requirement: Turn a streamed OpenAI chat completion into the final assistant message, including content and parallel tool calls whose fragments arrive interleaved.
skeleton: An IncompleteStreamError, ToolCall and Message dataclasses, and accumulate merging choice 0 deltas, grouping tool call fragments by index, requiring a finish_reason, and sorting calls by index.
caption: Rebuilding an OpenAI chat completion from streamed chunk dicts. accumulate(chunks) walks each chunk's choices, skipping any choice whose index is not 0 and tolerating chunks with empty choices such as a trailing usage chunk. Content deltas are appended, treating None as empty. Tool call fragments are merged by their index into ToolCall dataclasses: the id is kept from the first fragment that has one, and name and arguments fragments are concatenated. A truthy finish_reason is recorded on the Message. If none arrives it raises IncompleteStreamError, a RuntimeError; otherwise tool_calls are ordered by index. The fixture asserts that content deltas join into Hello with finish_reason stop, that interleaved calls come back as call_a search then call_b lookup with arguments that parse as JSON, that deltas from choice 1 are ignored, and that a stream without finish_reason raises IncompleteStreamError.

plan.intent: Support streaming responses in an agent loop
constraints: None content deltas count as empty
Tool call fragments are grouped by index and concatenated
The first non-empty id is kept

rationale.teaches: Streamed tool calls are keyed by index, not arrival order, and only the first fragment carries the id, so merge per index and keep state across chunks.
rationale.why: Overwriting instead of appending loses argument fragments, later null ids erase the real id, and ignoring the choice index mixes parallel completions.

ops.docstring: Accumulate streamed OpenAI chat completion chunks into one final message.

ops.source:
class IncompleteStreamError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the stream ends before any finish_reason arrives."""

candidates.why_wrong: Later fragments with a null id erase the tool call id.
Tool calls are returned in arrival order instead of by index.
Deltas from other choices are mixed into the first message.
A truncated stream is returned as if it had completed.
Each argument fragment overwrites the previous one, leaving invalid JSON.
